output.answer: As of today, Accenture's Chief Technology Officer is Dr. Marc Warner. He assumed the role on March 16, 2026, when Accenture completed its acquisition of Faculty, the UK applied-AI company he co-founded and still leads as CEO, and he joined Accenture's Global Management Committee. He succeeded Rajendra Prasad, who had been named Group Chief Executive—Technology and Chief Technology Officer in a June 20, 2025 reorganization (replacing the departing Karthik Narain) and now focuses on the Group Chief Executive—Technology role. Warner's CTO appointment was announced by Accenture itself, and his current Accenture leadership bio lists him as 'Chief Technology Officer, Accenture and Chief Executive Officer, Faculty.'
caveats: Marc Warner holds both roles simultaneously — Accenture CTO and CEO of Faculty — and his tenure is recent (March 16, 2026), so any change after that date would supersede this answer.
The prior CTO, Rajendra Prasad, remains Group Chief Executive—Technology; some outlets initially still listed Prasad as CTO around the transition period.

passages.quote: With the acquisition completed, Faculty CEO and co-founder Dr. Marc Warner expands his role to also become chief technology officer of Accenture and joins the company's Global Management Committee.
Dr. Marc Warner is the Global Chief Technology Officer of Accenture, where he is a member of the company's Global Management Committee, and CEO of Faculty.

Technology will be led by Rajendra Prasad, currently Accenture's Chief Information and Asset Engineering Officer, who will become Group Chief Executive—Technology and Chief Technology Officer. Prasad succeeds Karthik Narain, who has decided to leave Accenture to pursue other opportunities.

"I look forward to working with our new CTO Marc Warner to shape our technology strategy and execution and attract the best talent in the world to meet our clients' needs," said Julie Sweet, Accenture Chair and CEO.

output.question: Who is the CTO of Accenture?

key_facts.fact: Dr. Marc Warner (Faculty CEO and co-founder) became Accenture's Chief Technology Officer when Accenture completed its acquisition of Faculty, and joined Accenture's Global Management Committee.
Accenture's current leadership page lists Dr. Marc Warner as 'Chief Technology Officer, Accenture and Chief Executive Officer, Faculty' and a member of the Global Management Committee.

In Accenture's June 2025 growth-model reorganization, Rajendra Prasad became Group Chief Executive—Technology and Chief Technology Officer, succeeding Karthik Narain, who left the company; Prasad preceded Warner as CTO.
